part1.title: Text A
part1.text: Dear customers! We’d like to remind you that today, each of you can get a large bar of milk chocolate absolutely free. All you need to do is to buy three different products in our fruit and vegetables department. Please mind that dairy products like milk, cheese and cream, as well as meat products, like bacon or sausages, do not count. Visit our greengrocer’s, choose three tasty and healthy products there and get a bar of chocolate! Hurry — the number of chocolate bars is limited!

part1.title: Text B
part1.text: Hi, Mum! I’m just calling to say that I’m going to be home a bit later than usual. You know, we wrote a test in the morning and I think I did it successfully. After that, we decided to go to the cinema, as a whole class. A new film is on. I tried to contact you earlier, but the line was busy. You were having a conversation. I hope you won’t be angry with me that I’ve gone to the cinema without your permission. I have to mute my phone now and I’ll call as soon as I can.

lines.text: Oh, Mia! Yes, I was waiting for a friend, but he’s just called and said he’s not coming. We were going to the sports centre but now I don’t feel like going there alone.
Right. And I promised to meet my aunt at the station, but she’s missed her train and is coming on another one in three hours.
Which means you need to kill three hours.
Right. Look, there’s an art exhibition not far from here. Fancy going there together?
Oh, no! Art exhibitions are not for me. I’d rather go to the cinema. I don’t remember the name of the film, but I’ve heard it’s good.
Hello! You’re Ben Smith, aren’t you?
Yes, that’s me. I called you yesterday and you said that I could come today.
Right. I’ve read your CV. You say you are looking for a summer job.
Yes. My friend works for your pizzeria, and he says there are some vacancies for students here. He is on a gap year and he’s happy to have a job to support himself.
I see. And you are still at school, aren’t you?
Yes, it’s going to be my last year at school. After finishing it, I’m going to the university, I hope.
Great plan. OK. If this summer you want to deliver pizza to our customers, you are welcome.

part5.presenter: Good afternoon. Today we have asked 5 people to give us a short interview and share their opinions about their hometowns. Now we would like to present their opinions to you.

speakers.title: Speaker A
speakers.text: I was born in this town and have lived here all my life. It is situated along the river and there is a wonderful view of the water from my room. It is a lovely place to live in — very green and peaceful. There are few cars, as most people prefer bicycles, which is logical — the town is so small, you don’t need a car. You can cycle or walk wherever you want... For me, it’s the best place in the world though some of my friends dream of living in a big city.

speakers.title: Speaker B
speakers.text: I love my hometown. Historians say that it was founded more than 500 years ago. There were a few small houses, a mill and a church. There are several streets where you can still see traditional one- and two-storey houses and visit a history museum in the old mill. Now it’s a fast-developing industrial city. It has an electric power station that supplies the whole region, and a unique medical equipment manufacturing site.

speakers.title: Speaker C
speakers.text: My hometown is popular with tourists because of our cultural and historical events. For example, our annual autumn fair always attracts lots of people. We have been holding it since the 19th century, and it lasts for five days. The locals and tourists take part in different fair activities, win prizes, dance and enjoy the delicious food and fun games. Some people wear traditional costumes, which makes the whole event very colourful. Children and grandparents play games together!

speakers.title: Speaker D
speakers.text: I live in a big modern city with more than five million people. It’s not usually a problem to find a place to spend my free time. There are a lot of theatres, cinemas, clubs and other cultural and entertainment attractions. There’s always a wide choice of sports facilities and the career opportunities are good, which is very important for young people like my friends and me. I have a lot of friends and we often spend time together.

speakers.title: Speaker E
speakers.text: You know, we took a part in a city design competition recently. It was about how our town might look in fifty years’ time. My friends and I are interested in the city architecture and took it as a professional challenge. In our project, our town is based on smart technologies and artificial intelligence. It is very clean and green, only eco-friendly construction materials are used and there are no petrol cars in the streets. To me, it looks beautiful and we hope the jury will say the same.

part6.text: Thank you for agreeing to take part in our survey.
It’s OK. I’m glad to help.
You are fifteen, aren’t you? I just need to ask your age for the survey.
No, I’m still fourteen. I’m younger than my classmates.
Right. Fourteen. What’s your favourite subject if you have one?
I certainly have. I enjoy many subjects — Science is interesting and PE is fun. But if you want to know which I prefer the most, it’s Literature.
Do you think Literature may be important for your future career?
I don’t know. I just like reading. And I like writing essays, which most of my classmates hate.
Have you got a library at home?
Yes, a small one. Electronic books are convenient of course but I want to have at least a small amount of well-illustrated traditionally made books.
What does a small amount mean to you? How many books is it roughly?
Not roughly. There are exactly 80 books in my home collection at the moment. I hope there’ll be more.
Of course, there will. And what about sports and exercising? You said you enjoy PE lessons, which means you enjoy an active lifestyle.
Right. I like playing games — like football, basketball and even baseball sometimes. But what I do regularly is cycling.
Cycling? Do you find it boring?
I got used to it when my dog kept me company. With him it wasn’t boring at all. We both enjoyed our morning rides. But my dog passed away and now I cycle alone.
Sorry to hear that. Do you have any pets at the moment?
A snake. I knew you would be surprised.
I really am. I thought it was a puppy or a kitten.
I’ll adopt a puppy, but later. As for the snake, I got it from a friend who couldn’t keep it any longer. He moved to Australia but it’s a long story.
Australia? And what country would you like to visit in the near future?
Finland. I’ve never been to northern countries like Finland or Norway. Finland is the first on my list. Besides, I’ve got friends there. It would be nice to see them.

speaking.intro: Hello! It’s the electronic assistant of the new magazine Digital News. We kindly ask you to take part in our survey. We need to find out how people feel about their mobile phones. Please answer six questions. The survey is anonymous — you don’t have to give your name. So, let’s get started.
questions: How long have you had your mobile phone?
What do you use your mobile phone for?
In what public places do you normally turn off the sound of your mobile phone?
What other features of mobile phones do you find useful?
What would you miss most if you had to do without your mobile phone for a week?
How can people use a mobile phone to improve their foreign language skills?
speaking.outro: That is the end of the survey. Thank you very much for your cooperation.
